extra_misconceptions.fact: Safety is the active management of hazards to reduce risk to an acceptable level while still performing the activity.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Safety means eliminating every possible physical danger from an activity before any Scout is allowed to participate.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Personal protective equipment is the last line of defense after physically eliminating or substituting the hazard fails.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Wearing personal protective equipment such as gloves and goggles is the most effective first step in hazard control.

extra_misconceptions.fact: A hazard is a potential source of harm, whereas risk measures the likelihood and severity of harm from that hazard.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A hazard and a risk are identical terms that describe any dangerous object found around a home or Scout camp.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Warning signs are administrative controls that only alert people; mopping up the spill physically eliminates the hazard.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Posting a written warning sign next to a wet floor physically removes the slipping hazard for people walking by.

extra_socratic_questions: What distinguishes an unmitigated environmental hazard from the calculated probability of risk during a campout?
Which control level in the hierarchy of hazard management eliminates a threat completely rather than relying on gear?
Under what condition does personal protective equipment fail to reduce the underlying severity of a physical hazard?
Why is it dangerous to treat the temporary absence of accidents at a campsite as proof that hazards are controlled?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Sparklers burn at temperatures near 1,800 to 2,000 degrees Fahrenheit, which easily melts metals and ignites clothing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Consumer sparklers burn at a safe, low temperature that cannot ignite clothing or cause third-degree skin burns.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The test button primarily checks the battery and horn circuit, so alarms still require regular cleaning and ten-year replacement.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pressing the test button on a smoke alarm verifies that the internal smoke sensor chamber is clean and unobstructed.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Power strips are not rated for high-amperage heating appliances and can melt or ignite; plug space heaters directly into wall outlets.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Plugging a space heater into a heavy-duty power strip prevents household wall outlets from overheating and catching fire.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Carbon monoxide mixes evenly with room air and is completely undetectable without a dedicated electrochemical CO sensor.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Carbon monoxide gas rises to the ceiling immediately and triggers standard ionization smoke alarms throughout the house.

extra_socratic_questions: What measurement confirms that a residential water heater thermostat is set low enough to prevent scalding burns?
Why is it dangerous to pour water onto an ignited pan of cooking grease on a kitchen stovetop?
Where should a Scout position carbon monoxide and smoke detectors on each floor during a home safety inspection?
What happens to a consumer firework dud when someone approaches and attempts to relight its burned fuse?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Spring latches can be shimmed with a plastic card or forced open easily, whereas a one-inch deadbolt anchors deep into the framing.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A spring-loaded key-in-knob latch on an exterior door provides the same kick-in resistance as a one-inch throw deadbolt.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Short screws only grip the thin wooden door jamb trim; three-inch screws are required to anchor the strike plate into the wall stud.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Installing short half-inch brass screws in a door strike plate secures the lock against heavy physical force.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Dense shrubs right against windows give intruders concealed cover from neighbors and street traffic while they force a window open.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Tall privacy hedges planted right against first-floor windows deter burglars by blocking their view into the house.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Most home burglaries happen during daylight weekday hours when occupants are away at school or work.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Most residential burglaries occur late at night when every family member is asleep inside the home.

extra_socratic_questions: Which physical indicator on an exterior door frame shows that a deadbolt strike plate can resist forced entry?
What happens to exterior sightlines when overgrown shrubs block ground-floor windows from street visibility?
Where should a homeowner install a secondary wooden dowel or pin lock on a sliding glass patio door?
Under what condition does leaving a spare house key hidden under an outdoor welcome mat compromise home security?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Elevator shafts act as chimneys for toxic smoke and can lose power or open onto the fire floor; always use enclosed fire stairs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Hotel elevators are the fastest and safest evacuation route from upper floors when a building fire alarm sounds.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Tents and tarps offer zero lightning or wind protection; Scouts must move to a substantial building or hard-topped vehicle.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A large canvas dining fly or nylon dome tent beneath tall pine trees protects Scouts during a lightning storm at camp.

extra_misconceptions.fact: The Run, Hide, Fight protocol prioritizes evacuating immediately if a safe path exists, then barricading out of sight as a second option.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Pulling a fire alarm or playing dead on the floor is the recommended first response during an active shooter event.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Thick smoke quickly reduces hallway visibility to zero, requiring you to crawl low and count doors by touch to reach the exit stairs.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Counting the exact number of doors between your hotel room and the stairwell exit is unnecessary if hallways are lit.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to use an elevator instead of an enclosed stairwell when evacuating a burning hotel?
Where should a Scout patrol take shelter at camp when a severe thunderstorm or tornado warning is issued?
What happens to crowd flow in a stadium emergency if evacuees stop to retrieve personal bags or push against handrails?
Which specific details must you report to authorities when applying the phrase 'If You See Something, Say Something'?

extra_misconceptions.fact: No one-on-one contact is permitted inside rooms or tents; all interactions must stay in view of another adult or youth.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Two-deep leadership allows one registered adult leader to meet privately with a Scout inside a closed room or tent.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Youth sharing a tent must be no more than two years apart in age, and youth and adults never share a tent unless parent and child.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Youth Scouts of any age between 11 and 17 may share a tent at summer camp as long as they belong to the same patrol.

extra_misconceptions.fact: All digital communication between an adult leader and a youth must include a parent, guardian, or second registered adult leader.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Private text messages or direct social media messages between one adult leader and one Scout are allowed for troop planning.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scouts and leaders must report any suspected abuse or boundary violation immediately without trying to investigate it themselves.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Scout must wait until they have hard physical proof of abuse before reporting suspicious behavior to a trusted adult.

extra_socratic_questions: Under what condition does an electronic message or text from an adult leader violate Scouting's no one-on-one contact rule?
What age disparity limit applies when pairing Youth members together to share a tent at an overnight Scouting activity?
Which adult leadership composition is required before any Scouting trip, meeting, or merit badge session can take place?
Where should a Scout or parent report a suspected youth protection policy violation or boundary breach immediately?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many drink-spiking drugs are completely colorless, odorless, and tasteless, so you must replace any drink left unattended.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Drinks tampered with sedatives or illicit substances always change color, smell bitter, or look cloudy in the glass.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Isolated shortcuts remove witnesses and escape routes; always stay on well-lit streets with active pedestrian and vehicle traffic.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Cutting through an unlit alley or isolated parking lot is safer at night because it shortens the total walking distance.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Personal property can be replaced, so surrendering a bag and running toward a populated area is far safer than physical combat.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: If a stranger grabs your backpack or wallet on the street, fighting to keep your property is safer than letting it go.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Always maintain an independent way to get home, such as a charged phone, rideshare access, or a parent on standby.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Relying entirely on your date or party host for a ride home is safe as long as they promise not to drink alcohol.

extra_socratic_questions: Why is it dangerous to walk down a city street at night while wearing noise-canceling headphones and staring at a phone?
What happens to drink safety at a restaurant or party if you leave your glass unattended while visiting the restroom?
Where should you direct your steps if you suspect someone is following you on foot along a quiet residential block?
Which pre-arranged check-in and transportation backup plans protect teens when attending a social event or date?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Attackers use credential stuffing to test leaked passwords across banks and email, so every account needs a unique passphrase.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Using one complex password across all websites keeps your accounts safe even if one gaming forum suffers a data breach.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Recipients can capture screenshots, use a second camera, or recover cached files, making any shared digital image permanent.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Photos sent through disappearing-message apps vanish permanently from the internet and cannot be saved by the recipient.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Scammers easily spoof caller IDs and copy brand logos in phishing messages; verify requests only through official app or phone numbers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: An email or text that displays a company's official logo and caller ID name is guaranteed to come from that company.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unsecured public Wi-Fi lets attackers on the same network intercept unencrypted traffic; use cellular data or a trusted VPN instead.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Connecting to a free, open public Wi-Fi network at a cafe encrypts your login credentials and financial transactions.

extra_socratic_questions: Which technical barrier does multi-factor authentication add when a cybercriminal steals your account password?
What happens to embedded location metadata when you post an unedited smartphone photo publicly on social media?
Why is it dangerous to click a link inside an urgent text or email claiming your bank account is about to be locked?
Under what condition does forwarding or saving an explicit photo of a minor on a cell phone become a felony offense?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Unbelted back-seat passengers are thrown forward with deadly force in a crash, injuring both themselves and belted front occupants.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Passengers sitting in the back seat of a car or rideshare do not need seatbelts because the front seats cushion a crash.

extra_misconceptions.fact: An inflated vest inside a flooding cabin traps you against the ceiling and blocks the narrow exit; inflate it only after exiting.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Inflating your aviation life vest inside the airplane cabin helps you float out the emergency exit during a water landing.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Walk signals indicate right-of-way, not driver attention; pedestrians must make eye contact with drivers and look left-right-left.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A green pedestrian walk signal at a city intersection guarantees that turning drivers have seen you and stopped.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Always match the license plate, car make and model, and driver photo in your app, and ask the driver who they are picking up.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Getting into a rideshare car is safe as long as the driver waves at you and says they are picking up a passenger.

extra_socratic_questions: Which three identifiers must a passenger verify before opening the door and stepping into a rideshare vehicle?
Where should a commuter stand on a subway or train platform while waiting for an approaching train to stop?
Why is it dangerous to inflate a life vest inside a commercial airplane cabin before exiting through the emergency door?
What happens to passenger injury risk in a friend's truck if someone rides unrestrained in the open cargo bed?

extra_misconceptions.fact: Many safety technicians start through vocational certificates, fire academies, or apprenticeship programs before pursuing advanced degrees.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Every occupational safety career requires a university engineering degree before a candidate can enter the safety workforce.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Safety credentials require periodic recertification cycles backed by continuing education credits and annual renewal fees.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: A Certified Safety Professional credential remains valid for life without any ongoing training or recertification fees.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Field safety specialists spend much of their time conducting site walkthroughs, air sampling, noise testing, and worker drills.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Safety inspectors spend their entire workweek writing citations inside an office rather than testing hazards in the field.

extra_misconceptions.fact: Evaluating a career requires comparing total degree and licensing costs against regional job demand and advancement tiers.
extra_misconceptions.misconception: Starting salary figures alone determine whether a safety career path offers strong financial value to a new graduate.

extra_socratic_questions: What verification step must a Scout complete with a parent before scheduling a workplace interview with a safety officer?
Which daily workplace duties distinguish a Certified Industrial Hygienist from a general occupational safety specialist?
What specific tuition, certification exam, and continuing education metrics belong in your career pathway cost comparison log?
Why is it dangerous to tour an active industrial job site during a career interview without verified personal protective gear?
